issue: Has letting residents vote on the budget led to better decisions for the estate?
background:
A town council set aside $500,000 of its yearly improvement budget for residents to decide. Residents proposed projects. Every household could then vote, online or at a booth beside the market, over two weeks in March.

The three projects with the most votes were built: a covered walkway, a fitness corner and a new playground. About one in seven households voted. The council is now deciding whether to hold the vote again next year with a bigger sum.

title: Raising the price of water
issue: Was raising the price of water the right decision?
background:
The national water agency raised the price of water by 20% in two steps, the first on 1 July. It was the first rise in twelve years. The agency said that water now costs more to produce, because more of it comes from treating sea water and used water.

Households in smaller flats were given rebates on their bills. Shops, stalls and factories paid the new price in full. Some people welcomed the rise as a way to make everyone save water. Others said it was unfair.

title: Closing a neighbourhood school with few pupils
issue: Is closing the school the best choice for its pupils?
